parts.title: A Model with a Free Spirit
parts.directions: Read the passage and choose the best answer (A, B, C, or D) for each question.
passage: Many people imagine that a model's life is full of glamour, expensive clothes and famous names. Linh, a twenty-three-year-old model from a small coastal town, says that the reality is different, and that the most important thing for her is freedom. Her story began when a photographer noticed her at a local festival, but she soon learned that being noticed was only the beginning. This text is an imagined profile, but it is based on real facts about the modelling industry and shows why some young people choose this uncertain career.

Modelling became a profession in 1853, when the designer Charles Frederick Worth asked his wife to wear his designs for customers. Today there are many kinds of work, including fashion shows, magazine photographs, fitness advertising and even parts modelling, in which only the hands or feet appear in the picture. Some models are tall and slim for runway work, while others, such as plus-size and fit models, are chosen because their bodies match the sizes that clothing companies need. Linh prefers jobs that are **flexible**, because she can choose her own travel dates and also accept short projects from different companies. She says that this variety keeps her curious and stops her from getting bored.

The job is not always easy. Most models work part-time, and one source says that only about 3,200 models in the United States work full-time, while the median income there in 2021 was about 34,000 dollars a year. For this reason, many models may need a second job to pay their bills. Because work can disappear suddenly, Linh saves part of every payment and keeps her costs low. Days can also be **exhausting**, with early flights, long waits between photographs and repeated changes of clothes and make-up.

Linh does not wait for an agency, because she likes to plan her own projects. She works with a young photographer **who** shares her love of travel, and together they plan short trips to nearby islands and mountain villages, where they create their own pictures for magazines and websites. She also uses social media to show her style, although she warns that online followers can bring pressure as well as opportunities. Her advice to beginners is to read every contract carefully and to say no to anything that feels unsafe.

Linh believes that models must also look after their health. Very thin body ideals have been criticised, and Vogue reportedly banned models under sixteen in 2012. In 2013, New York passed a law that requires at least twelve hours between shifts for young models and an adult chaperone for those under sixteen. Linh hopes that the industry will keep changing. For her, being a model means using her image to earn a living without losing her own voice, her curiosity or her freedom.

parts.title: Understanding Left-Handedness
parts.directions: Read the passage and choose the best answer (A, B, C, or D) for each question.
passage: Roughly nine in ten people are right-handed, which means that about one in ten is left-handed. Handedness is usually defined by the writing hand, although many people are mixed-handed, and true ambidexterity, in which both hands work equally well, affects only about one per cent. This passage examines what research suggests about why handedness arises and what it does and does not imply.

Handedness is not distributed equally between the sexes, although the difference is **modest**. A 1975 study of 7,688 American schoolchildren found that 9.6 per cent were left-handed, including 10.5 per cent of boys and 8.7 per cent of girls. A later meta-analysis of 144 studies, covering nearly 1.8 million participants, reported that men were about 23 per cent more likely than women to be left-handed. Figures of this kind vary slightly between studies, countries and age groups.

The causes of handedness are **multifaceted**. Twin studies suggest that genes explain only about a quarter of the variation, and researchers estimate that at least forty genetic loci contribute, so no single gene decides the matter. If both parents are left-handed, the chance that a child is also left-handed is about 26 per cent. Prenatal influences have also been proposed, including exposure to certain drugs and, more weakly, ultrasound scanning, but the evidence remains limited.

Because language is usually controlled by the left hemisphere, some researchers have linked handedness to brain lateralisation. The picture is less simple than that, however, since most left-handers also rely mainly on the left hemisphere for language, and only about 30 per cent do not. Handedness and language dominance are therefore related but not identical. Preferences emerge early, with one source reporting that 39 per cent of infants favour one hand between six and fourteen months and 97 per cent of toddlers do so by the age of two.

Left-handedness has long carried a stigma. In English and many other languages, the word for right also means correct. Left-handed children were often forced to write with their right hands, a practice reported in Soviet schools, in parts of Uganda and even in the childhood of King George VI. Many everyday tools, from scissors to corkscrews, are designed for right-handers, but left-handers have to use **these** every day.

Left-handers are overrepresented in some sports, with about half of fencers and roughly forty per cent of seeded tennis players being left-handed, probably because opponents rarely practise against them. Claims about intelligence and income are less consistent. A 2018 meta-analysis found that right-handers scored only about 1.5 IQ points higher, a negligible difference. Studies of earnings have reached opposite conclusions, with one suggesting a premium for college-educated left-handers and another a lifetime penalty. Health associations, such as a higher risk of Parkinson's disease among left-handed women, are reported but remain tentative.

Taken together, the evidence suggests that left-handedness is a natural and ordinary variation shaped by many genes and by environment, not a defect or a gift. International Left-Handers Day, held every 13 August since 1992, now celebrates a difference that was once stigmatised. The most useful lesson is that people should be judged on what they do, not on which hand they use to do it.

options.A: Left-handers are cleverer and healthier than others because their brains work differently
options.B: Handedness is determined by one gene that parents always pass to children

options.A: Genes explain nearly all the variation between identical twins
options.B: Identical twins always share the same hand preference as parents
options.C: Genes explain only about a quarter of the variation
options.D: Environment has no effect once a child starts school

options.A: perfectly obvious
options.B: strictly limited
options.C: easily measured

questions.stem: The word "these" in paragraph 5 refers to _______.

options.A: right-handers
options.B: everyday tools
options.C: Soviet schools
options.D: left-handers

questions.explanation: Đọc ngược câu chứa đại từ "these" ở đoạn 5. options.B: Both hemispheres equally, with no dominant side at all
options.C: Mainly the left hemisphere, as most right-handers do
options.D: The cerebellum, which also controls balance and body posture

options.A: A clear link between left-handedness and artistic genius
options.B: Left-handers making up about half of all fencing participants
options.C: Opposite findings from various studies of left-handers' lifetime pay
options.D: A negligible average IQ difference in favour of right-handers

Chi tiết về "mối liên hệ rõ ràng giữa việc thuận tay trái và thiên tài nghệ thuật" hoàn toàn không được đề cập trong bài.

options.A: Left-handers are certain to excel at sport because opponents are rarely prepared
options.B: Handedness probably reflects many small influences, so strong claims about talents are unreliable
options.C: Parents who are left-handed will inevitably have children who are left-handed too
options.D: Language dominance in the brain fully determines which hand a person prefers

options.A: To persuade parents to train left-handed children to use their right hands
options.B: To prove that left-handers are more creative than right-handers in many fields

parts.directions: Read the passage and choose the best answer (A, B, C, or D) for each question.
passage: Cities across Southeast Asia have spent the past four decades building rail systems, and the region now offers a revealing case study in how **burgeoning** metropolises respond to congestion. Some networks opened in the 1980s, while others carried their first passengers only in the past few years. This passage examines how the systems differ, what limits their growth and why riders have not always followed the tracks.

Manila's Light Rail Transit opened in 1984, and Singapore's Mass Rapid Transit followed in 1987, making both among the oldest urban rail networks in the whole region. **[1]** Kuala Lumpur and Bangkok joined them in the 1990s, with service starting in 1996 and 1999 respectively. [2] Singapore, in particular, is often described as following a state-led planning model in which one authority coordinates routes, stations and surrounding housing. **[3]** That reliability helped the system reach about 146 stations and roughly 247 kilometres of track, and it carried about 1,240 million journeys in 2024, although figures vary by method. **[4]** Bangkok, by contrast, ended up with separate systems run by different operators, and the lack of ticket integration is a frequent complaint among riders.

Latecomers have followed a different path. Jakarta opened its MRT in 2019, Hanoi began operating its first metro in 2021, and Ho Chi Minh City opened a line of about 19.7 kilometres with 14 stations in 2024. These lines are short beside Singapore's network, and several cities are reportedly planning extensions.

Ridership shows how uneven the picture is. Singapore's network reportedly carried about 1,240 million journeys in 2024, Kuala Lumpur's about 330 million in 2025 and Bangkok's BTS about 267 million in 2024. The two Vietnamese systems recorded roughly 20 million journeys each, far fewer than **those** of the older networks, partly because the lines are young and short. These comparisons need care, since operators count transfers in different ways and some figures were affected by COVID-19.

Building a metro is only half of the task, because a line is useful only if people can reach its stations. In many cities, pavements are narrow or crowded, so motorbikes may seem quicker for short trips. Planners therefore try to link rail with feeder buses, walkways and park-and-ride sites, so that passengers can complete the first and last kilometre without a car.

Money is the other constraint, and it shapes almost every decision about routes and timing. Metro construction is expensive, and the cost of tunnelling beneath crowded streets can rise sharply when contracts, land purchases or utilities are disputed. As a result, progress in several countries has been **incremental**, with a few kilometres added every few years rather than whole networks opened at once.

Taken together, the region's rail networks show that success depends on planning, integration and patience as much as on tunnels and trains. The older networks have already shown what steady public investment can achieve, while the newer ones may need a decade or more to influence daily travel habits. For commuters, the real test is whether a journey by rail becomes easier than the alternatives.

parts.title: The Evolutionary Trajectory of Monetary Systems
parts.directions: Read the passage and choose the best answer (A, B, C, or D) for each question.
passage: Money is so **ubiquitous** that its history is easily mistaken for a straight line from shells to smartphones. In reality, the evolution of monetary systems has been uneven, contested and repeatedly reversed, with each new form of money resolving one problem while creating another. This passage traces that trajectory, from early debates about origins to the digital currencies of the present.

Adam Smith's account, in which people first bartered goods and later invented money to escape the difficulty of finding a partner with matching needs, has long been influential. **[1]** Carl Menger developed the argument by suggesting that the time spent searching for barter partners pushed societies towards common media of exchange. **[2]** Anthropologists are far more sceptical, and Caroline Humphrey found no example of a pure barter economy. **[3]** David Graeber, drawing on Mitchell Innes's 1913 essay, offers a different interpretation, arguing that money began as a unit of account in which a casual promise became a quantified debt. **[4]** That reversal matters because it shifts attention from coins and commodities to trust, record-keeping and the social obligations that money represents.

Whatever its origins, money soon took physical form. Mesopotamian shekels, first recorded around 2150 BC, were nominally equal to a fixed weight of barley, while cowrie shells served as currency in parts of ancient China, Africa and India. Coinage came later, with Lydian electrum coins of about the seventh century BC regarded as ancestors of modern coins, and bronze knives and spades circulating in China from around 1000 BC. These objects shared one feature, namely that their value rested on a material that people already wanted.

The next major innovation was paper money, which appeared first in China. During the Tang dynasty, merchants' deposit receipts acted as a precursor of banknotes, and the Song dynasty later issued the first generally circulating notes, called jiaozi, in the eleventh century. By the early twelfth century, the notes issued in a single year reportedly reached 26 million strings of cash, and news of the idea travelled to Europe through travellers' accounts, including that of Marco Polo.

In Europe, banknotes appeared much later than in China and proved fragile at first. Stockholms Banco, **whose** notes of 1661 are generally regarded as the first in Europe, stopped operating in 1664 after running out of coins to redeem them. The Bank of Scotland began printing notes in 1696, and the Bank of England gained sole rights to issue notes in England after 1694. Stability came when national banks guaranteed to convert silver money into gold at a fixed rate, although the Bank of England nearly failed in the 1730s.

The link between money and gold, however, did not survive the twentieth century. In 1971, Richard Nixon ended the direct convertibility of the United States dollar into gold, an act that effectively destroyed the Bretton Woods system, and national currencies became free-floating. Fiat money, which has only nominal value, therefore depends on trust in the state, and exchange rates have tended to be more **volatile** since then. Meanwhile, by 1990 all money moved between the American central bank and commercial banks electronically, and by the 2000s most money existed as digital entries in bank databases.

The most recent chapter began in 2008, when Satoshi Nakamoto proposed Bitcoin, a decentralised peer-to-peer currency built on a blockchain ledger that solved the double-spending problem without a trusted third party. Whether these currencies will rival state money remains uncertain, since price swings and regulation both limit their use as everyday means of payment. The history of money is a history of changing answers to the question of whom to trust.

tasks.guide_md:
**1. Phân tích đề bài và xác định dạng đề:**
- Đây là dạng **Formal Email** (email trang trọng) vì người nhận là quản lí nhà sách. Bạn cần sử dụng ngôn ngữ lịch sự, chuyên nghiệp và tránh các cách diễn đạt quá thân mật.
- Đề yêu cầu trả lời 3 nội dung chính: dịch vụ yêu thích tại nhà sách, thể loại sách thường đọc và đề xuất cải thiện chất lượng dịch vụ.
- Bài viết cần tối thiểu **120 từ**. Cần đảm bảo phản hồi đầy đủ các ý thay vì chỉ mô tả trải nghiệm cá nhân.

**2. Cách xây dựng bố cục logic (Organization):**
- **Greeting:** Sử dụng cách chào trang trọng. Ví dụ: Dear Bookstore Manager,
- **Opening:** Giới thiệu mục đích viết thư. Ví dụ: I am writing to share my feedback about your bookstore services.
- **Body:** Nên chia thành 2 đoạn: đoạn đầu nói về dịch vụ yêu thích và sở thích đọc sách, đoạn sau đưa ra đề xuất cải thiện.
- **Closing:** Kết thúc bằng lời cảm ơn và mong nhận được sự cải thiện trong tương lai. Ví dụ: I appreciate your efforts and hope my suggestions will be useful.
- **Sign-off:** Dùng cách kết thúc lịch sự như Yours sincerely hoặc Best regards.

**3. Chiến lược đạt điểm cao (Vocabulary & Grammar):**
- Sử dụng thì hiện tại đơn để mô tả dịch vụ hiện tại và thói quen đọc sách.
- Sử dụng cấu trúc lịch sự như I would like to suggest hoặc I believe that để đưa ra ý kiến.
- Tránh chỉ liệt kê ý tưởng; hãy giải thích lý do tại sao bạn thích một dịch vụ hoặc tại sao đề xuất đó hữu ích.
Từ vựng quan trọng:
- **Customer service:** Dịch vụ khách hàng
- **Book selection:** Sự lựa chọn sách
- **Reading habits:** Thói quen đọc sách
- **Self-help books:** Sách phát triển bản thân
- **Fiction novels:** Tiểu thuyết hư cấu
- **Service quality:** Chất lượng dịch vụ
Từ nối (Linking words):
- **Firstly:** Thứ nhất
- **In addition:** Ngoài ra
- **Moreover:** Hơn nữa
- **However:** Tuy nhiên
- **Therefore:** Vì vậy
Cách diễn đạt cảm xúc (Expressing feelings):
- **I am impressed by:** Tôi ấn tượng bởi
- **I really appreciate:** Tôi rất đánh giá cao
- **I am satisfied with:** Tôi hài lòng với

**4. Các lỗi thường gặp:**
- Viết email quá thân mật với các cụm như Hi hoặc Thanks a lot trong thư gửi quản lí.
- Không đưa ra đề xuất cụ thể mà chỉ nói chung chung như improve services.
- Quên sử dụng ngôn ngữ lịch sự khi đưa ra góp ý.

**5. Cách kiểm tra bài trong 2 phút cuối:**
- Kiểm tra đã có mở đầu và kết thúc phù hợp với email trang trọng chưa.
- Đảm bảo đã trả lời đủ ba yêu cầu trong đề bài.
- Kiểm tra lỗi chia động từ, từ vựng và số lượng từ.

**6. Tư duy làm bài:**
Hãy viết như một khách hàng đang gửi phản hồi chuyên nghiệp. Mục tiêu không phải dùng từ quá khó mà là thể hiện ý kiến rõ ràng, lịch sự và có tính xây dựng.

tasks.guide_md:
**1. Phân tích đề bài và xác định dạng bài:**
- Đây là dạng bài **Cause–Effect Essay**. Bạn cần phân tích nguyên nhân gây ra căng thẳng ở giới trẻ và những ảnh hưởng của vấn đề này.
- Từ khóa quan trọng là **stress**, **young people**, **causes** và **effects**. Không nên chỉ tập trung vào giải pháp vì đề không yêu cầu.
- Bài viết cần tối thiểu **250 từ**, cần có luận điểm rõ ràng, giải thích nguyên nhân và đưa ra ví dụ phù hợp.

**2. Cách xây dựng bố cục (Organization):**
- **Introduction:** Giới thiệu vấn đề stress ở giới trẻ và nêu hướng triển khai bài. Ví dụ: Stress has become a significant concern among young people today.
- **Body 1:** Phân tích các nguyên nhân. Có thể đề cập áp lực học tập, công việc, tài chính hoặc ảnh hưởng từ mạng xã hội. Ví dụ: One major cause of stress is the pressure to achieve academic success.
- **Body 2:** Phân tích ảnh hưởng của stress đến sức khỏe, học tập và các mối quan hệ. Ví dụ: Excessive stress can negatively affect both mental and physical health.
- **Body 3 (nếu cần):** Có thể mở rộng bằng cách giải thích mối liên hệ giữa nguyên nhân và hậu quả.
- **Conclusion:** Tóm tắt nguyên nhân và tác động chính. Ví dụ: In conclusion, stress among young people is caused by various factors and can lead to serious consequences.

**3. Chiến lược đạt điểm cao (Vocabulary & Grammar):**
- Sử dụng hiện tại đơn để nói về vấn đề phổ biến trong xã hội.
- Phát triển ý theo cấu trúc Cause -> Explanation -> Example -> Effect để đoạn văn có chiều sâu.
- Cần có câu chủ đề rõ ràng cho từng đoạn và tránh lặp lại từ stress quá nhiều lần.
Từ vựng quan trọng:
- **Academic pressure:** Áp lực học tập
- **Workload:** Khối lượng công việc
- **Financial problems:** Vấn đề tài chính
- **Mental health:** Sức khỏe tinh thần
- **Emotional pressure:** Áp lực cảm xúc
- **Social expectations:** Kỳ vọng xã hội
Từ nối (Linking words):
- **One of the main reasons is:** Một trong những nguyên nhân chính là
- **Furthermore:** Hơn nữa
- **As a result:** Kết quả là
- **For instance:** Ví dụ
- **Consequently:** Do đó
- **In conclusion:** Tóm lại
Diễn đạt lại ý (Paraphrasing):
- **Young generation:** Thế hệ trẻ, thay cho young people.
- **Psychological pressure:** Áp lực tâm lý, thay cho stress.
- **Negative consequences:** Hậu quả tiêu cực, thay cho bad effects.
Cách diễn đạt ý kiến / so sánh / giải pháp:
- **It is widely recognized that:** Được công nhận rộng rãi rằng, dùng để mở bài.
- **This problem can be attributed to:** Vấn đề này có thể bắt nguồn từ, dùng để nói nguyên nhân.
- **This leads to:** Điều này dẫn đến, dùng để trình bày hậu quả.

**4. Các lỗi thường gặp:**
- Viết cả bài về nguyên nhân nhưng không phân tích tác động.
- Đưa ra quá nhiều nguyên nhân nhưng không giải thích cụ thể.
- Sử dụng ví dụ không liên quan hoặc quá cá nhân mà thiếu tính khái quát.

**5. Cách kiểm tra bài trong 3–5 phút cuối:**
- Kiểm tra đã đề cập cả causes và effects chưa.
- Đảm bảo mỗi đoạn thân bài có câu chủ đề rõ ràng.
- Kiểm tra lỗi ngữ pháp, chính tả và số lượng từ tối thiểu 250 từ.

**6. Tư duy làm bài:**
Hãy tập trung xây dựng mối liên hệ logic giữa nguyên nhân và hậu quả. Một bài viết có ý tưởng rõ ràng, ví dụ phù hợp và bố cục chặt chẽ sẽ hiệu quả hơn việc sử dụng quá nhiều từ vựng khó.

**1. Phân tích đề bài:**

- **Topic A (Dancing):** Các câu hỏi 1–3 tập trung vào sở thích, thói quen và lợi ích của việc nhảy múa. Bạn cần thể hiện khả năng nói về hoạt động giải trí và sức khỏe.
- **Topic B (Self-care):** Các câu hỏi 4–6 nói về việc chăm sóc bản thân, lối sống lành mạnh và cách duy trì sức khỏe thể chất, tinh thần.
- Tiêu chí chấm điểm gồm **Fluency, Vocabulary, Grammar và Pronunciation**. Bạn cần phát triển câu trả lời bằng lý do và ví dụ thay vì chỉ trả lời một câu ngắn.
- Nên dành khoảng **25–35 giây cho mỗi câu hỏi** để cân bằng thời gian giữa hai chủ đề.

**2. Cách xây dựng bố cục khi nói (Organization):**
- Sử dụng cấu trúc **Answer – Reason – Example (ARE)**: trả lời trực tiếp -> giải thích -> đưa ví dụ.
- **Ví dụ Topic A:** I enjoy dancing because it helps me relax and stay healthy. For example, I often dance to my favorite songs after a long day.
- **Ví dụ Topic B:** I usually take care of myself by exercising and getting enough sleep because these habits improve my health.
- Luôn tự hỏi thêm **Why?** hoặc **How?** để mở rộng câu trả lời.
- Khi chuyển chủ đề, có thể dùng câu nối như: Besides my hobbies, I would like to talk about how I take care of myself.
